title: Superlative adjectives
summaryText: Use a superlative to say that one person or thing has the most (or least) of a quality in a group.

rows: long → the longest · tall → the tallest
Double the last consonant, then add **-est**
the best feature · the worst singer

examples: I am the tallest in my family.
This box is the biggest one.
My house is the largest one in our neighborhood.
This exam is the easiest one.
This is the most famous dish.
It is the most interesting movie in my life.

practiceExercises.prompt: I am ______ in my family. (tall)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: I am the tallest in my family.

practiceExercises.prompt: This box is ______ one. (big)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: This box is the biggest one.

practiceExercises.prompt: My house is ______ one in our neighborhood. (large)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: My house is the largest one in our neighborhood.

practiceExercises.prompt: This exam is ______ one. (easy)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: This exam is the easiest one.

practiceExercises.prompt: This is ______ dish. (famous)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: This is the most famous dish.

practiceExercises.prompt: It is ______ movie in my life. (interesting)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: It is the most interesting movie in my life.

title: Future: *will* vs. *going to*

rows: **Instant decisions** (decided while speaking). *I will buy some milk after work.*
**Plans / intentions** (already decided before speaking). *I'm going to buy some milk after work.*
**Opinion** (we think something will happen). *They won't win their next match.*
**Based on evidence** (we can see it now). *Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.*

patterns: Useful pattern for opinion + decision: **I think I'll …** / **I don't think I'll …** + verb
examples: It's cold today. I don't think I'll go out.
I'm hungry. I think I'll have something to eat.

practiceExercises.prompt: Look at those clouds. It is ______ rain. (Prediction based on evidence)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.

practiceExercises.prompt: They ______ win their next match. (Opinion prediction: we think something will happen)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: They won't win their next match.

practiceExercises.prompt: It's cold today. I don't think I'll ______ out.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: It's cold today. I don't think I'll go out.

practiceExercises.prompt: I'm hungry. I think I'll ______ something to eat.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: I'm hungry. I think I'll have something to eat.

rows: Can you lend me your smartphone?
Of course. Here you are! / Sure. Here you go.

practiceExercises.prompt: ______ I borrow your pen?
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: Could I borrow your pen?

practiceExercises.prompt: ______ you lend me your smartphone?
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: Can you lend me your smartphone?

practiceExercises.prompt: Please ______ me go out.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: Please let me go out.

practiceExercises.prompt: When responding to a request with agreement, you can say: "Of course. ______ you are!"
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: Of course. Here you are! / Sure. Here you go.

title: Word-level language points in Unit 7
notes: **Suffix -ible / -able** (Lesson 1): both make adjectives. *-ible* cannot stand alone (possible – poss); *-able* can stand alone (suitable – suit).
**Parts of speech** (Lesson 2): noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, preposition.
**Adjectives in a product review** (Lesson 5): use adjectives to help the reader understand your opinion.
Lesson 3 (video lesson) has no new grammar target.

title: Present perfect
summaryText: **Use:** to describe an action that began in the past and continues in the present. Lesson 3 also practices *Have you ever …?* (life experience) as a warm-up.

rows: S + have / has + V past participle
They have learned English for 2 years.
S + have / has + not + V past participle
They have not met each other since 1999.
Have / Has + S + V past participle?
Have you completed the final exam?

examples: People have played cards for about twelve hundred years.
Players have created about one hundred different solitaire games.
Many players haven't played solitaire with cards since computers became popular.
How often have you played it? · How many times have you won?
Warm-up: Have you ever eaten sushi? → Yes, I have.

practiceExercises.prompt: They ______ (learn) English for 2 years.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: They have learned English for 2 years.

practiceExercises.prompt: They ______ (not meet) each other since 1999.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: They have not met each other since 1999.

practiceExercises.prompt: ______ you completed the final exam?
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: Have you completed the final exam?

practiceExercises.prompt: People ______ (play) cards for about twelve hundred years.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: People have played cards for about twelve hundred years.

practiceExercises.prompt: ______ you ever eaten sushi? → Yes, I have.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: Have you ever eaten sushi? → Yes, I have.

rows: We have talked for 30 minutes in the class. · It has rained for a week.
I have waited here since 9 a.m. · My parents have lived in Vietnam since 1980.

practiceExercises.prompt: We have talked ______ 30 minutes in the class.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: We have talked for 30 minutes in the class.

practiceExercises.prompt: It has rained ______ a week.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: It has rained for a week.

practiceExercises.prompt: I have waited here ______ 9 a.m.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: I have waited here since 9 a.m.

practiceExercises.prompt: My parents have lived in Vietnam ______ 1980.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: My parents have lived in Vietnam since 1980.

title: Cause and effect

rows: She is never interested in studying because she wants to become a basketball player.
I don't think he wants to attend the party since he is an introvert.
It rained, so I got wet.
She used to play taekwondo. As a result, she knows how to defend herself.

patterns: Note: *since* has two meanings. With a time (since 1980) it is a starting point; with a clause (since he is an introvert) it means *because*.

practiceExercises.prompt: She is never interested in studying ______ she wants to become a basketball player.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: She is never interested in studying because she wants to become a basketball player.

practiceExercises.prompt: I don't think he wants to attend the party ______ he is an introvert.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: I don't think he wants to attend the party since he is an introvert.

practiceExercises.prompt: It rained, ______ I got wet.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: It rained, so I got wet.

practiceExercises.prompt: She used to play taekwondo. ______, she knows how to defend herself.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: She used to play taekwondo. As a result, she knows how to defend herself.

title: *There* + *to be*
summaryText: Use *there* + *to be* to say that something exists or happens. The verb agrees with the noun that follows.

rows: There are twenty chairs in the classroom.
There were three worms in my salad.
There has been / There have been
There have been many earthquakes in this century.
There will be an excellent party next weekend.
There is / are going to be
There are going to be fireworks at the festival.

practiceExercises.prompt: ______ twenty chairs in the classroom. (Present)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: There are twenty chairs in the classroom.

practiceExercises.prompt: ______ three worms in my salad. (Past)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: There were three worms in my salad.

practiceExercises.prompt: ______ many earthquakes in this century. (Present perfect)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: There have been many earthquakes in this century.

practiceExercises.prompt: ______ an excellent party next weekend. (Future with will)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: There will be an excellent party next weekend.

practiceExercises.prompt: ______ fireworks at the festival. (Future with going to)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: There are going to be fireworks at the festival.

title: WH-questions
summaryText: WH-questions ask for specific information. The answer is not just *yes* or *no*.

rows: What is this? – It's a book.
Where do you live? – I live in Hanoi.
When do you go to school? – In the morning.
Why do you like to eat apples? – Because they are sweet.
Who do you love the most? – My mom.
People (object of the verb or preposition)
With whom am I speaking? – You are speaking with Lisa.
Which color do you prefer to wear? – Pink.
Manner, condition, quality; also distance, length, quantity, age
How old are you? – I'm 11 years old.

patterns: The lesson practices turning a statement into a question in different tenses:
examples: What is she doing in her room? (present continuous)
When do they play soccer? (present simple)
What did Tom buy last week? (past simple)
When will the concert start? (future with *will*)
Where are we going this weekend? (*going to* / present continuous)
How long has he been working at a software company? (present perfect continuous)

practiceExercises.prompt: ______ is this? – It's a book. (Asks about things/objects)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: What is this? – It's a book.

practiceExercises.prompt: ______ do you live? – I live in Hanoi. (Asks about place)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: Where do you live? – I live in Hanoi.

practiceExercises.prompt: ______ do you go to school? – In the morning. (Asks about time)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: When do you go to school? – In the morning.

practiceExercises.prompt: ______ do you like to eat apples? – Because they are sweet. (Asks about reason)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: Why do you like to eat apples? – Because they are sweet.

practiceExercises.prompt: With ______ am I speaking? – You are speaking with Lisa. (Object of preposition)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: With whom am I speaking? – You are speaking with Lisa.

practiceExercises.prompt: ______ color do you prefer to wear? – Pink. (Making a choice)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: Which color do you prefer to wear? – Pink.

title: Talking about likes and dislikes
summaryText: Examples: Eating healthy food is my favorite. · I don't like staying up late.

rows: I don't mind … / … doesn't bother me. (neutral)

patterns: After these expressions, the lesson examples use a noun or a verb + **-ing**.

practiceExercises.prompt: Eating healthy food is my ______.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: Eating healthy food is my favorite.

practiceExercises.prompt: I don't like ______ up late. (Note: use noun or verb + -ing)
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: I don't like staying up late.

practiceExercises.prompt: I am really ______ playing mobile games.
practiceExercises.sourceSentence: I am (really) into …

title: Other language points in Unit 8
notes: **Suffix -ful** (Lesson 1): noun + -ful → adjective meaning "full of" or "characteristic of" (help → helpful, wonder → wonderful, thank → thankful, joy → joyful, peace → peaceful).

**Contrast connectors in the writing model** (Lesson 5): *Unlike …, Instead, However, both … and …*, used to compare how different places celebrate the summer solstice. The model also uses *There have been … since ancient times* (present perfect).
Lesson 3 (video lesson) has no new grammar target beyond the *Have you ever …?* warm-up.
